title: Lightweight GPU dependency virtualization and canary benchmarking harness
creator: Ava Chen
description:
Summary:
Introduce a small virtualization layer for GPU runtime dependencies that provides deterministic resolution and safe rollback semantics for mixed-driver/mixed-cutlass fleets. The shim will be intentionally minimal: a manifest-driven resolver + per-kernel contract checker that sits between container start and runtime kernel binder. The goal is to reduce cold-start probe jitter, provide an A/B canary path for new kernel bundles, and give engineers a reproducible local testing harness for quantized kernels without requiring full repackage or heavy client-side rebuilds.

Motivation / Background:
- We see intermittent OOM/fallbacks and probe-time variability across fleets when new cutlass/triton bundles land. This increases tail latency for short lived workloads and forces conservative version pinning.
- Existing approaches (full repackage, binary grafting) are heavy and slow to iterate. We need a low-risk, easily revertible layer that can: 1) enforce simple ABI contracts (symbol presence + capability tags), 2) order fallbacks deterministically, and 3) enable lightweight canary benchmarking before rolling to Dedicated/Hosted.

Scope / Non-goals:
- Scope: implement the virtualization shim, manifest schema, runtime resolver, CI canary job, micro-benchmark harness, and telemetry hooks (probe latency, symbol-resolution errors, chosen bundle).
- Non-goal: do not attempt to replace full kernel bundling or packaging flow; this is a runtime compatibility surface to reduce incidents and speed rollouts.

Design notes:
- Manifest: JSON manifest per kernel-bundle with fields: bundle_id, driver_min, driver_max, symbols:[{name, semantic_tag}], heuristic_score, fallback_order. Will be validated by CI linter.
- Resolver: deterministic selection by (customer_policy -> bundle_score -> health-> fallback_order). No randomization: reproducible per-host decisions for easier debugging.
- ABI contract checker: runs symbol-existence checks and a small sanity microkernel (self-check op) to catch obvious incompatibilities before binding. Time budget: 50ms warmup budget; anything longer causes resolver to mark bundle degraded.
- Canary benchmarking: per-deploy canary percentage and a microbench suite (latency p50/p95, small batch throughput, kv-cache hit impact). Canary job in CI will run the microbench on synthetic traces and compare against baseline thresholds.
- Rollback: deterministic frozen manifest version for a release; in failure cases the resolver will auto-fallback to pinned bundle and increment a telemetry counter. Rollback via flag in console to repoint fleet-level manifest.

Acceptance criteria:
1) Shim loads and resolves bundle manifest on startup.
2) Resolver produces same selection given same host metadata in 100% of runs in integration tests.
3) Canary microbench pipeline in CI passes and blocks merges if p95 regression > 10% or error rate increase > 0.5%.
4) Telemetry surface emitted to console: probe_latency_ms, chosen_bundle, fallback_count, contract_failures.

Implementation plan / milestones:
- Week 1: Prototype shim and manifest schema; local dev harness to simulate two competing bundles. (Owner: Diego)
- Week 2: Add ABI contract checker and short microkernel health check; integrate basic telemetry. (Owner: Diego)
- Week 3: CI canary job + gating script + PR to runtime repo; generate baseline microbench corpus. (Owner: CI Eng)
- Week 4: Dogfood on staging Dedicated region with 5% canary; collect telemetry and iterate on heuristics. (Owner: SRE)
- Week 5: Roll to 25% with automated rollback enabled; create runbook for operators. (Owner: SE/Oncall)

Progress updates / decisions so far:
- 2026-01-13: Spike complete. Prototype shim implemented in C++ with a 1.2KB manifest parser. Initial microkernel uses a tiny GEMM-ish sanity op compatible with quant backends. Observed deterministic selection across repeated starts.
- 2026-01-18: Trade-off: we considered a dynamic linker interposition approach (LD_PRELOAD) but rejected due to security review and complexity in sandboxed VMs; we'll use a loader hook at our runtime entrypoint instead.
- 2026-01-22: Contract checker threshold set to 50ms for warmup probe; ops that exceed threshold mark bundle "degraded" and trigger fallback. This threshold chosen from 95th percentile of existing probe durations.
- 2026-01-29: Added telemetry dimensions to trace: resolver_decision_reason and manifest_checksum. Feedback from Runtime leads indicates these are sufficient to triage.

Open risks / mitigations:
- Risk: Manifests drift across teams and become authoritative single source of truth. Mitigation: CI linter and manifest signing; require PR review on manifest changes for any release.
- Risk: Microbench synthetic trace doesn't represent true customer mixes. Mitigation: include sampled short-sequence traces from production (anonymized) in benchmark corpus with opt-out.
- Risk: Extra startup cost on very short-lived containers. Mitigation: allow pinned-bundle fast-path that skips contract checker when explicit pin exists and a signature is verified.

- Design doc: https://docs.redwood.ai/confluence/display/RUNTIME/Lightweight+GPU+Dependency+Virtualization

Reviewer notes / requested feedback:
- Need SRE signoff on rollback runbook before staging canary.
- Security: ask platform infra for brief review about loader hook vector.
- Runtime team: confirm microkernel op is representative enough for quant kernels (CC: Priya Rao).

Next actions (short):
- Create runtime PR with shim and manifest linter (in progress).
- Add canary CI job and baseline corpus (blocked: CI quota for GPU minutes).
- Draft rollback runbook and SRE playbook (owner: Diego).

Done when: shim merged, CI canary job gating merged, staging canary run at 5% with telemetry showing no regressions for 72 hours, runbook approved.
